verses: And the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
Let the people of Israel also keep the Passover at its appointed season.
On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you shall keep it in its appointed season: according to all its rites, and according to all its ceremonies, you shall keep it.
And Moses spoke to the people of Israel, that they should keep the Passover.
And they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month at twilight in the wilderness of Sinai; according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so did the people of Israel.
# And there were certain men who were defiled by the dead body of a man, so that they could not keep the Passover on that day; and they came before Moses and before Aaron on that day:
And those men said to him, We are defiled by the dead body of a man; why are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the LORD in its appointed season among the people of Israel?
And Moses said to them, Stand still, and I will hear what the LORD will command concerning you.
# And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
Speak to the people of Israel, saying, If any man of you or of your descendants is unclean by reason of a dead body, or is on a journey far off, yet he must keep the Passover to the LORD.
The fourteenth day of the second month at twilight they shall keep it, and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They must leave none of it until the morning, nor break any bone of it; according to all the ordinances of the Passover they must keep it.

But the man who is clean and is not on a journey, and refuses to keep the Passover, that same person must be cut off from his people, because he did not bring the LORD's offering at its appointed time; that man must bear his sin.

If a stranger lives among you and keeps the Passover to the LORD, according to the Passover ordinance and its manner, he must do so; you must have one ordinance for both the stranger and the native-born.
# And on the day the tabernacle was erected, the cloud covered the tabernacle, that is, the tent of the testimony; and in the evening there was on the tabernacle something like a fire, until morning.
Thus it was always: the cloud covered it by day, and the fire appeared by night.
When the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, the children of Israel then journeyed; and wherever the cloud stayed, the children of Israel pitched their tents.
By the LORD's command the children of Israel journeyed, and by the LORD's command they pitched; as long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, they rested in their tents.
When the cloud lingered long over the tabernacle for many days, the children of Israel kept the LORD's command and did not journey.
Thus it was when the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for a few days; by the LORD's command they remained in their tents, and by the LORD's command they journeyed.
Thus it was when the cloud stayed from evening until morning, and when the cloud was taken up in the morning, they journeyed; whether the cloud was taken up by day or by night, they journeyed.

Whether it was two days, a month, or a year that the cloud lingered over the tabernacle, remaining there, the children of Israel stayed in their tents and did not journey; but when it was taken up, they journeyed.
By the LORD's command they rested in the tents, and by the LORD's command they journeyed; they kept the LORD's command, by the LORD's command through Moses' hand.
